correctness.rationale: For \(n\ge4\), same-shore selected pairs force at least one opposite-shore omission. At the extremal two-omission level, explicit adjacency to the unique outside middle vertex yields exactly \(i,j>t\) or \(i=j\le t\). The latter fails for \(t\ge2\) because a remaining matched nonedge needs an outside three-edge geodesic through the deleted edge, and works exactly at \(t=1\). The former always works by explicit geodesics and connectedness. For \(t=n\), two omissions fail and three omissions give exactly two mirror complement patterns. Counting these labelled patterns proves every branch. Independent brute graph enumeration compares all maxima as sets for \(4\le n\le7\) and all extremal candidates for \(n=8\), with no extrapolation used as proof.

value.rationale: Balanced biclique matching deletion is a natural sparse perturbation of a classical family. The exact connected-geodesic optimum remains rigidly \(2n-2\) until complete deletion, yet its maximizing configurations collapse from \(n^2\) to one at \(n-1\) deletions; deleting the last matching edge lowers the maximum and creates \(2n(n-1)\) configurations. The \(t=1\) anomalous extra optimizer and complete structural classification are genuinely parameter-sensitive, motivated infinite-family results not obtained by plugging a single number into a known theorem.
